title: Claude Code builds and self-corrects a Unity explosion effect by checking captured frames
summary: A game developer had Claude Code build a Unity explosion effect; the agent captured and reviewed frames and kept fixing it without help, the author says, sharing first and final versions.
agent_role: Claude Code created the particle system, captured rendered frames, inspected them and revised the effect on its own. The human set the task and supplied textures made with Codex image generation.
outcome: The author shared first and final versions in the thread, showing the agent's iterations.
what_they_did: A developer gave Claude Code a game visual-effects task: build an explosion in Unity using the Shuriken particle system. The agent built the effect, captured frames of it, checked them, and kept making fixes on its own. The textures were made separately with Codex image generation.
how_it_went: The author says the agent kept fixing the effect without help and posted the first and final versions side by side in the thread.
worth_knowing: The key piece is the capture-and-review loop: the agent improves the effect by looking at rendered frames rather than only editing settings blind.
prompt: In my Unity project at [project path], build a [effect type, e.g. explosion] using the Shuriken particle system. Use the textures in [texture folder]. After each change, play the effect, capture several frames and review them against this goal: [describe the look, timing and colors]. List what looks wrong and fix it, then repeat until it matches or you have done [number] rounds. Show me the first and latest frames and a summary of the changes before you modify any existing prefabs or scenes.

curation.rationale: A genuine agent loop: Claude Code built a Unity particle effect, captured frames, checked them visually and kept fixing it. The idea is novel for game VFX, but the post is very short and the only evidence is a before/after video.
